name: kind_prediction_v2

metrics.name: coverage
metrics.note: guard against shrinking to look precise

metrics.name: accuracy_on_placed
metrics.note: read at tolerance 0.035 = one error on ~31 placements

rationale: SEAL 3 on domain B. NOT a re-cut of `kind_prediction`: that seal and its REGRESSED verdict stand permanently, and the lift-weighting change is NOT retroactively re-judged by this one. Baseline here is the CURRENT post-lift state, so this seal judges FUTURE substrate work only. WHY A SECOND SEAL WAS NEEDED: the first registered `accuracy_on_placed` at tolerance 0, and that metric is MECHANICALLY COUPLED to coverage -- going from 22 placements to 31 while holding `wrong` at exactly 2 is near impossible, so the seal was structurally hostile to the improvement it was written to detect. That was a fault in how I registered it, of the same class as V7-2's absolute bar sitting below chance: a threshold set without knowing the measurement's natural variance. THE TOLERANCE IS DERIVED, NOT CHOSEN: on ~31 placements a single wrong answer moves accuracy by 1/31 = 0.032, so measurements of this seal are to be taken at tolerance 0.035 -- exactly one error's worth of movement and no more. HARNESS GAP, stated because it is real: `measure()` takes the tolerance as an argument and the seal does not store it, so this figure is sealed only in this text. A future harness should carry it in the manifest. THE SIGNATURE THIS SEAL LOOKS FOR: `correct` RISES WHILE `wrong` DOES NOT. That is 'better, not merely looser', and it is deliberately strict enough that the change which produced this baseline (correct 20->28, wrong 2->3) would ALSO have failed it -- so nothing here is arranged to rescue work already measured.
